title: Washington Sets the Pattern
objective: After this level you can explain the precedents Washington set as the first president, from the cabinet to stepping down after two terms.
summary: Washington, the only president elected unanimously, created the cabinet, took no royal title and retired after two terms. Ona Judge, enslaved in his household, escaped in 1796.

cards.headline: The first president had to decide even what to be called.
cards.body: Every choice Washington made could become a rule for the future. One woman in his household made a choice of her own.

cards.headline: The first everything
cards.body: George Washington is the only president elected unanimously by the Electoral College, in both 1789 and 1792. With no one before him, every choice set a pattern. One of the most lasting was creating the president’s cabinet.

cards.headline: No royal titles
cards.body: The Senate proposed calling him “His Highness the President of the United States of America and Protector of their Liberties.” The House rejected any title, and the Senate gave way. A plain title suited a republic.

cards.headline: Knowing when to leave
cards.body: Washington retired after two terms, a precedent every president followed until Franklin D. Roosevelt. In his Farewell Address of 1796, he warned against “the baneful effects of the spirit of party.” Walking away from power was itself the lesson.

cards.headline: Ona Judge’s own precedent
cards.body: The pattern had another side. On May 21, 1796, Ona Judge, a woman the Washingtons enslaved, escaped from the President’s House in Philadelphia while they ate dinner. She had learned Martha Washington planned to give her to a granddaughter. Washington tried to have her recaptured, but she lived the rest of her life in New Hampshire, legally still a fugitive, until her death in 1848.

cards.headline: Washington Sets the Pattern: explained
learned: Washington: the only president elected unanimously
He created the cabinet and accepted no royal title
He retired after two terms and warned against party spirit
Ona Judge escaped the President’s House in 1796

questions.prompt: Which precedent did Washington set when he left the presidency?

options.label: Choosing his own successor
options.rationale: His precedent was stepping down after two terms.

questions.explanation: Washington retired after two terms, a pattern that held until Franklin D. Roosevelt.

questions.prompt: How was the question of the president’s title settled?

options.label: The Senate’s grand title was adopted
The House refused any title; the Senate agreed

questions.explanation: The Senate wanted “His Highness”; the House refused any title, and the Senate gave way.

questions.prompt: Ona Judge fled to New Hampshire, yet remained legally a fugitive. Which part of the Constitution from Level 33 let enslavers claim people who escaped to another state?

options.label: The three-fifths clause
options.rationale: That counted people for House seats and taxes.

questions.explanation: The fugitive clause said a person held to service who escaped to another state must be delivered up on claim.
